questions.stem: The exchange rate is $\text{£1} = \text{R8}$. The beam is level when both sides give the same number of rand for each pound. Drag the right pan until it is level: how many rand is $\text{£2}$ worth?

pending_review.why: This predicate fires when the student levels the beam by matching products, 1 x 8 = 2 x d, which puts the right pan at 4. That is a direct-versus-inverse proportion confusion ('more pounds, so fewer rand'). The claimed misconception is about multiplying or dividing by the rate the wrong way round. A student who divides £2 by the rate gets 2 / 8 = 0.25, not 4. The beam cannot show 0.25 because it only takes whole numbers from 1 to 24, so that error would not fire this predicate. Reaching 4 means dividing the rate by the amount (8 / 2) or reasoning that more pounds buy fewer rand, which is not the stated operation-direction slip. The predicate would mostly fire for a different reason, so matches is false.

canonical_solution.text_md: The exchange rate $\text{£1} = \text{R8}$ says that every pound is worth the same R8, so the rand per pound is fixed.
The beam is level when both sides show that same rate: $\text{£1} : \text{R8} = \text{£2} : \text{R}?$.
$\text{£2}$ is two lots of $\text{£1}$, so the rand side must be two lots of $\text{R8}$.
To find the cost in rand, multiply the foreign amount by the rate: $2 \times 8 = 16$, so drag the right pan to $\text{R16}$.
Check: $\text{R16} \div 2 = \text{R8}$ for each pound, the same rate as on the left, so the beam is level.
